column3: NASB follows the critical text with “wine” and “was unwilling.”
NASB follows the critical text; the fulfillment quotation (“They divided My garments …”) is from the Textus Receptus.
“Were denigrating” is rendered “were hurling abuse at.”
NASB follows the critical text with a statement (“He is the King of Israel”), without “if.”
NASB renders “wants Him” as “delights in Him,” adds “God,” and prints the Old Testament wording in capitals.
NASB renders “were upbraiding Him” as “were also insulting Him with the same words.”
NASB prints the cry in capitals as an Old Testament quotation.
NASB omits “Wait!”; the added sentence about the spear (in some manuscripts) is not included.
NASB omits nothing significant; “was shaken” is rendered “shook.”
NASB follows the critical text with “Joseph.”
NASB follows the critical text and adds “to him.”
